item.title: Current Events - November 11, 2026
item.description:
November 11, 2026 (2026-11-11) (Wednesday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • 2026 Iran war
    • 2026 Iranian strikes on Oman
      • Iran attacks ship navigation systems on Didamar Island, Oman. Unknown damage is caused. (Reuters)
  • Gaza war
    • Attacks on health facilities during the Gaza war
      • Israel launches an airstrike against the Nasser Medical Complex in Khan Younis, killing six Palestinians, including a surgeon, and wounding over 20 more. Four more people are also killed in other airstrikes in the Gaza Strip. (Al Jazeera) (Reuters)
  • Allied Democratic Forces insurgency, Ituri war
    • At least 22 people are killed by Islamic State-affiliated Allied Democratic Forces rebels across eight locations in Mambasa Territory, Ituri Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo. (AP)
  • Insurgency in Jammu and Kashmir
    • Three Central Reserve Police Force personnel are injured after militants open fire on a checkpoint near Mir Bazar in Kulgam district, Jammu and Kashmir, India. Security forces launch a search operation to locate the attackers. (Gulf News) (The Hindu)
  • Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
    • Pakistani Taliban carries out an ambush against police personnel in Kohat District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, killing ten officers. Eighteen gunmen are also killed in the ensuing shootout. (AP)

Business and economy

  • 2026 Iran war fuel crisis, German economic crisis
    • The German cabinet approves draft legislation establishing a strategic natural gas reserve of 24 terawatt-hours, equivalent to approximately 10% of national storage capacity, to maintain gas supplies during emergencies. (AFP via France 24)
  • 2026 Paraguay banking crisis
    • The Central Bank of Paraguay reports providing partial refunds to 1,812,348 eligible Ueno Bank depositors following the Ueno's collapse. (France 24)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026–27 European windstorm season
    • Portugal closes approximately 8,000 schools nationwide and suspends non-essential public services as Storm Charles approaches. The second day of the Web Summit in Lisbon is also cancelled. (AP) (Deadline)
  • 2026 New York City building collapse
    • A 3-story apartment building collapses near a construction site in Brooklyn, New York City, United States, killing eight people and wounding 19 more. (AFP) (Reuters)

Health and environment

  • 2026 Ebola epidemic
    • The Kenyan health ministry reports that the country has discharged its last Ebola patient from a hospital in Nairobi after eleven contact cases were treated. Kenya will be declared Ebola-free on December 23 if no one else exhibits symptoms. (DW)
    • The number of confirmed Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo surpasses 11,000, with at least 5,387 deaths, affecting 8 of the country's 26 provinces. (Al Jazeera)
  • The American ocean liner SS United States is sunk off the coast of Destin–Fort Walton Beach, Florida, United States, to become the world's largest artificial reef. (Pensacola News Journal) (Reuters)

International relations

  • Argentina–Iran relations
    • Iran designates the Argentinian naval and air forces as terrorist organizations, in response to Argentina designating the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps as such in March. (Al Jazeera) (Reuters)
  • China–Germany relations
    • Germany announces that its military will discontinue using Chinese-made drones for military training and exercises, replacing them with German or other European models to address security concerns. (AP) (Reuters)
  • France–Russia relations
    • Russia bans two French lawmakers, Arthur Delaporte and Sacha Houlié, and two journalists, Ariane Chemin and Paul Gogo, from entering the country for allegedly harassing Xenia Fedorova, the head of RT France, from 2017 to 2023. (Al Jazeera)
  • Kenya–Sudan relations
    • Kenyan president William Ruto signs a deal for Sudan to lift its 20-month ban on imports of tea from Kenya. (Business Daily Africa)

Law and crime

  • 2026 European infrastructure disruption
    • European bomb threat wave
      • More than 6,000 schools across Italy are evacuated following bomb threats. (BBC News) (Reuters)
  • Colombian conflict
    • Two people are arrested in connection with an explosive attack on the headquarters of Colombian broadcaster RCN Televisión in Cali, Valle del Cauca. (AFP via Gulf News)
  • Former Red Brigades member Leonardo Bertulazzi escapes house arrest in Buenos Aires, Argentina, while awaiting extradition to Italy to serve a 27-year prison sentence for kidnapping and membership in an armed group. Argentine security forces launch a manhunt for him. (AFP via France 24)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 United States Senate elections
    • 2026 United States Senate election in Mississippi
      • After a week of counting affidavit ballots, the Associated Press and CNN project the election to the U.S. Senate in Mississippi for Democratic candidate Scott Colom, defeating the incumbent Republican Cindy Hyde-Smith and becoming the first black senator from the state since Blanche Bruce in the 1874–75 elections. (AFP) (AP) (CNN)
  • 2026 Brazilian general election
    • The Brazilian Superior Electoral Court fines Meta Platforms R$7.5 million (US$1.34 million) for failing to comply with judicial orders concerning the 2026 presidential election, while finding insufficient evidence of deliberate electoral interference. (AFP via Le Monde)
  • 2026 Spanish housing protests
    • Millions of workers across Spain launch a general strike to demand government intervention over the country's housing crisis, as an escalation of the ongoing protests. (Al Jazeera) (El País)
  • Gibran Rakabuming Raka diploma controversy
    • Indonesian vice president Gibran Rakabuming Raka submits his resignation amid questions about his educational qualifications. Bloomberg News reports that President Prabowo Subianto accepts the resignation, although the government has not publicly confirmed its acceptance. (Reuters)
  • Independence March
    • Polish president Karol Nawrocki and at least 500,000 people participate in the annual patriotic march celebrating the National Independence Day in Warsaw, Poland. (Zero in Polish)

Science and technology

  • Cyberwarfare by Russia
    • The Romanian Intelligence Service (SRI) reports that it stopped a December 2025 cyberattack against an unidentified government institution, attributing it to the Russia-linked trojan package Turla. The SRI finds no evidence that sensitive information was stolen. (Reuters)
  • Cybersecurity firm CloudSek reports that the Kazakhstan-linked hacker group Silent Lynx used an autonomous agent to breach Tajikistan's government database and steal more than 2,000 national security-related documents. (The Record) (Reuters)

Sports

  • 2026 FIFA U-17 World Cup
    • The United States men's national under-17 soccer team withdraws from the upcoming FIFA U-17 World Cup in Qatar, citing safety concerns related to the Houthi–Saudi conflict. (AFP) (ESPN)

item.title: Current Events - November 04, 2026
item.description:
November 4, 2026 (2026-11-04) (Wednesday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • 2026 Bangladesh garment workers protests
    • Over 50 people are injured and police vehicles are torched as garment workers clash with police in Savar. (The Financial Express)
  • Sudanese civil war
    • War crimes in the Sudanese civil war, Kordofan campaign
      • Two women are killed in a airstrike by Sudan's army on a water source in Umm Badr, North Kordofan. (Sudan Tribune)

Business and economy

  • 2026 Bangladesh garment workers protests
    • The Bangladeshi garment industry wage board agrees to increase minimum wages following five days of worker protests and clashes with police. Workers demand ৳30,000 (US$240) monthly, up from ৳12,500 (US$100), while the board has not specified the increase. (AFP)

Disasters and accidents

  • Five people are killed while two others are injured in an explosion at a suspected illegal fireworks factory in Malasiqui, Pangasinan, Philippines. (The Philippine Star)
  • A fire and explosion at a Panasonic subsidiary's factory in Hsinchu County, Taiwan, kills two employees and injures five others. (Reuters)

Health and environment

  • 2026 Southeast Asian haze
    • The Singaporean parliament amends the Transboundary Haze Pollution Act of 2014, introducing arrest powers, permitting trials in absentia, and increasing maximum fines tenfold to S$20 million (US$15 million) following widespread air pollution from Indonesian wildfires. (AFP)
  • The United Kingdom's Office for National Statistics reports that deaths linked to cocaine use have overtaken deaths from heroin in England and Wales for the first time on record. The increase in deaths from cocaine use is blamed on increased purity of the drug and its widespread availability across the UK in recent years. (BBC News)

Law and crime

  • Illegal drug trade in the Philippines
    • Philippine authorities seize a 200-kilogram (440 lb) shipment of methamphetamine, whose origin is traced to Laos, at the Manila International Container Port. The shipment had arrived six days after Laotian police found similar contraband destined for the Philippines. (Arab News) (Philippine Daily Inquirer)
  • Former American internet personality and YouTuber Bryant Moreland (known online as EDP445) is arrested in Las Vegas, Nevada, U.S., on multiple felony sex crime charges following self-incriminating statements made in a recent documentary by American director Mike Clum including a 2021 incident in Bakersfield, California. (The New York Times) (The Hindustan Times)
  • Hackers steal approximately €100 million (US$112 million) from French bank Crédit Mutuel through unauthorized transactions using the bank's account. (Firstpost)
  • President of the Bolivian Supreme Court Romer Saucedo announces that he is leaving the country following an investigation into drug trafficking in which senior judicial officials, such as former Attorney General Roger Mariaca, have been arrested. (La Tercera)

Politics and elections

  • Hungary makes Communist-era secret police records publicly accessible through a database containing approximately 60,000 names linked to former state security services. Prime Minister Péter Magyar announces that additional documents will become available in February 2027. (Reuters)

Science and technology

  • The Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory, a space telescope for studying gamma-ray bursts, re-enters Earth's atmosphere over Sumatra, ending its mission of nearly 22 years. (NASA)

item.title: Current Events - November 10, 2026
item.description:
November 10, 2026 (2026-11-10) (Tuesday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Peace negotiations in the Russo-Ukrainian war, United Arab Emirates in the 2026 Iran war, United States and the Russo-Ukrainian war
      • 2026 United States–Ukraine–Russia meetings in Abu Dhabi
        • A third round of United States-mediated talks between Ukrainian and Russian delegations begins in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, focusing on the humanitarian impact of the war, prisoners of war, and security guarantees. Earlier in the day, the American and Ukrainian teams held a separate meeting with representatives of France, Germany, Italy, the United Kingdom, the European Commission, and NATO. (AP) (DW) (The Guardian)
  • Haitian conflict
    • Salvadoran military intervention in Haiti, El Salvador–Haiti relations
      • El Salvador announces it has launched a joint military operation with the Haitian police against the 400 Mawozo gang, killing 20 people and destroying a house linked to its leader, Wilson Joseph. (Al Jazeera)
  • Democratic Republic of the Congo–Rwanda conflict
    • A military court in Goma, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo, sentences 66 soldiers to death on charges of cowardice, mutiny, and failure to obey orders, after they were arrested following clashes with Front for the Refoundation of the Nation rebels. (DW)
  • Terrorism in Kenya, Somali Civil War
    • Eight people, including five workers and two police reservists, are killed by suspected al-Shabaab militants in Mandera County, Kenya, near the border with Somalia, during an ambush against a vehicle. (AFP via AA) (Reuters)

Business and economy

  • Energy crisis in Venezuela
    • The Venezuelan National Assembly unanimously approves a reform of the electricity law which allows private companies and joint ventures to invest in the nationalised electricity sector, which the government has controlled since 2007. (AFP via RFI)
  • The Monetary Authority of Singapore launches a gold reserve service for foreign central banks, international financial institutions, and sovereign entities, and announces expanded tax exemptions for wholesale gold services. (AFP via The Daily Star) (Reuters)

Disasters and accidents

  • Eleven people are killed and at least 50 others are seriously injured in a multiple-vehicle collision involving 86 trucks and cars [bg] on the Trakia A1 motorway near Yambol, Bulgaria. (Al Jazeera) (Plovdiv24)
  • Five schoolgirls are killed and 21 others are injured when a school bus plunges into a pond in Kandal province, Cambodia. (AP)
  • The British Columbia Conservation Officer Service kills a female grizzly bear and her three cubs after DNA evidence confirmed that the bears killed two people near Bella Coola, B.C., Canada. (AFP via ABS-CBN News) (BBC News)

Health and environment

  • AI boom
    • The Thai cabinet approves new environmental regulations for data centers, including limits on noise and temperature increases, requirements for cooling-water recycling and testing, and industrial zoning for facilities consuming more than 20 megawatts. (AFP via The Straits Times)
  • The United States Food and Drug Administration orders manufacturers of GLP-1 medicines such as semaglutide and tirzepatide, originally intended for the treatment of type 2 diabetes but also commonly used for weight loss, to add warnings that use of such drugs may increase the risk of developing non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, an optic nerve disorder that can cause permanent blindness. (BBC News) (Reuters)

Law and crime

  • 2025–2026 Indonesian protests
    • Indonesian police detain 154 people following clashes with protesters in Yogyakarta, Java. The Yogyakarta Legal Aid Institute reports that two people are hospitalized and 13 others remain missing. (AFP via New Straits Times)
  • LGBTQ rights in Trinidad and Tobago
    • The Judicial Committee of the Privy Council overturns colonial-era provisions criminalizing consensual same-sex sexual activity between adults in Trinidad and Tobago, ruling them unconstitutional following a legal challenge by activist Jason Jones. (CNN) (Reuters)
  • United Kingdom–United States relations, Russia–United Kingdom relations
    • Police arrest an American soldier near Gloucester, England, on suspicions of espionage activity in connection with Russia. (DW)
  • An explosive device kills a police officer and his K9 dog and injures another while they were responding to a shooting in Oviedo, Asturias, Spain. (AP) (BBC News)
  • British news outlets The Guardian and ITV News identify comedian and author David Walliams as the subject of sexual misconduct allegations after the High Court of Justice rejects his attempt to prevent their publication. Walliams denies the allegations. (CNN) (RTÉ News)

Politics and elections

  • Gibran Rakabuming Raka diploma controversy
    • Indonesian vice president Gibran Rakabuming Raka announces his intention to resign following controversies about the authenticity of his high-school diploma. (Reuters)

Science and technology

  • AI boom
    • Australian prime minister Anthony Albanese announces plans to introduce mandatory safeguards for artificial intelligence companies, including security incident reporting and independent model evaluations, and establish a new regulatory body to oversee compliance. (AFP) (ABC News)

item.title: Current Events - November 03, 2026
item.description:
November 3, 2026 (2026-11-03) (Tuesday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • 2026 Iran war
    • 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
      • A commercial vessel is hit by an unidentified object in the waters of Musandam Governorate, Oman, killing an Indian crew member, while 13 others are rescued. (Reuters)
  • 2026 Bangladesh garment workers protests
    • A 21-year-old garment worker dies from injuries sustained the previous day during violent clashes with law enforcement in Gazipur. (The Independent)
    • Ten police officers are injured in clashes between police and garment workers in Dhaka over low pay and the rising cost of living. (Dhaka Tribune)
  • Communal conflicts in Nigeria
    • Unidentified attackers ambush a police convoy near Gidan-Giye village in Zamfara State, Nigeria, killing at least five police officers and three members of the Zamfara Community Protection Guard, injuring two officers, and abducting an unspecified number of personnel. (Reuters)

Arts and culture

  • Spanish author Cristina Fernández Cubas is awarded the 2026 Cervantes Prize to honor her writing in the Spanish language. (Euronews)

Business and economy

  • 2026 Iran war fuel crisis
    • The Reserve Bank of Australia raises its benchmark interest rate by 0.25 percentage points to 4.85%, its highest level since 2008, citing persistent inflation and rising energy costs associated with the Iran war. (AFP via France 24)

Disasters and accidents

  • Two helicopters operated by Air Dynasty and Fishtail Air collide while landing in Solukhumbu District, Nepal, near Mount Everest, killing an Indian tourist and injuring a New Zealand national. (AFP via Times of Malta)

Law and crime

  • Five suspected robbers, including two former police personnel, are killed in shootouts with police in Bacoor, Cavite, Philippines. (Daily Tribune)
  • Three people are arrested for allegedly wiretapping Indonesian president Prabowo Subianto's phone. (AFP via South China Morning Post)
  • Bomb hoaxes target seven flights from several European countries. (BBC News)
  • The Israeli cruise ship MS Crown Iris is targeted by a false bomb threat, and is searched on Syros, Greece. (Reuters)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 United States elections
    • The United States holds midterm elections for 435 members and five non-voting delegates of the House of Representatives, 35 members of the Senate (including special elections in Florida and Ohio), 39 state and territorial governors, and numerous other state, territorial, tribal, and local officials. (The Guardian)
    • U.S. news organizations project that the Democratic Party will control the House of Representatives and the Senate in the upcoming 120th Congress, ending the Republican Party's majority in both chambers. (Reuters) (The Guardian)
    • Several states elect their first Democratic representatives in decades, including: Adam Hamilton, the first Democrat to win a Kansas Senate seat since 1932; James Talarico, the first Democrat to win a Texas Senate seat since 1988; and Gina Hinojosa, the first Democrat to become governor of Texas since 1990. (NBC News) (Axios)
    • Abdul El-Sayed defeats Mike Rogers in the United States Senate election in Michigan, making him the first Muslim to be elected to the U.S. Senate. (The Washington Post) (Time)
    • Keisha Lance Bottoms defeats Rick Jackson in the gubernatorial election in Georgia, becoming the first black woman to be elected governor in U.S. history. (AP)
  • Spanish transport minister Óscar Puente resigns after the country experienced two train collision disasters in one year, the Adamuz derailment in January and the Toledo collision last week, which had a combined casualty toll of 115 deaths and 492 injuries. (CNN)

Sports

  • 2026–27 Segunda División
    • In association football, CD Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel dies following an in-game collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono the previous day. (CNN)
  • 2026 Melbourne Cup
    • In thoroughbred racing, Point Of Law, trained by Ciaron Maher, wins the 2026 Melbourne Cup at Flemington Racecourse in Victoria, Australia. Zahrann and Juja Kibo, also trained by Maher, finish second and third respectively. (AFP)
  • 2027 AFC Asian Cup, Houthi–Saudi conflict
    • In association football, the Asian Football Confederation postpones the 2027 Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia from January 2027 to January 2028, citing security concerns and travel disruptions following Houthi attacks on the country. (AFP via France 24)

item.title: Current Events - November 12, 2026
item.description:
November 12, 2026 (2026-11-12) (Thursday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • At least 10 people, including five with gunshot wounds, are injured in Munshiganj Sadar, Bangladesh during a clash involving gunfire and crude bomb explosions between two factions of the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party. (The Business Standard)

Business and economy

  • Nvidia alleged spying scandal
    • Jensen Huang resigns as chief executive officer (CEO) and president of Nvidia and leaves the company's board following reports of two extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese intelligence agent. Chief financial officer Colette Kress becomes interim CEO. (AFP) (Reuters)

Health and environment

  • 2026 Bangladesh measles outbreak
    • Four more children in Bangladesh are reported to be killed from measles, bringing the death toll past 1,299. (BSS)

Law and crime

  • Iranian external operations
    • A British court convicts two Iranian men of spying on journalists from London-based broadcaster Iran International. One of them is also convicted of preparing a violent attack, while a third defendant is acquitted. (AFP via RFI) (AP)
  • Mass shootings in the United States
    • At least five people are shot, including one fatally, in Logan Circle, Washington D.C., United States. The suspected gunman later kills himself after barricading himself from police inside a nearby apartment. (Al Jazeera) (AP)

item.title: Current Events - November 05, 2026
item.description:
November 5, 2026 (2026-11-05) (Thursday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • A police officer is killed and another injured in a stabbing attack outside the Sri Lankan embassy in Amman, Jordan. The suspect is arrested. The event is described as a terrorist attack. (Ammon News) (Al Jazeera)

Business and economy

  • Mexico approves the Digital Economy Act for Digital and Electronic Payments, which allows it to designate sectors in which digital payments are the only accepted means of payment. (N+ in Spanish)

Disasters and accidents

  • Eleven people are killed and 33 more injured after the collision of a passenger bus with a truck in Pakpattan District, Punjab, Pakistan. (AP)
  • Six people are killed and nine more injured after a fire at a two-story home in Brooklyn, New York City, United States. (AP) (Sky News)
  • Six more people are found dead under the debris of a building that collapsed two weeks ago in Nairobi, Kenya, bringing the death toll to eight. Sixteen others are still missing. (AP)

Law and crime

  • 2026 Afyonkarahisar shootings
    • Eight people are killed and another is injured in a shooting spree at three separated locations in Afyonkarahisar Province, Turkey. The perpetrator is arrested. (AP)
  • Cannabis in Nepal
    • The Nepali supreme court directs the government to regulate cannabis cultivation for medicinal, scientific, agricultural, horticultural, and industrial purposes. (AFP via France 24)
  • Koldo affair
    • Six people are arrested in connection with a corruption investigation involving ruling PSOE officials and the transport ministry in Spain. (Ara)
  • Cuban authorities release independent journalist Yoani Sánchez and activists Berta Soler and María Cristina Labrada after detaining them for several hours in Havana. (AFP)
  • The Hong Kong High Court sentences pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong to an additional 10 years in prison under the national security law for conspiring with foreign entities to impose sanctions against China and Hong Kong. (AFP)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 European unrest
    • 2026 French student protests, Yellow vests protests
      • The syndicate of unions organizes a general strike across France, supported by the yellow vests movement, activists, and student protesters. (CNN)
  • 2026 Grenadian general election
    • Grenadians vote to elect 15 members of the House of Representatives. Incumbent prime minister Dickon Mitchell wins a second consecutive NDC government, with opposition NNP leader Emmalin Pierre losing her seat in St. Andrew South East. (AP) (St. Vincent Times)
  • 2026 Paraguay banking crisis
    • Paraguayan president Santiago Peña announces his resignation after the collapse of ueno bank, and the Chamber of Deputies unanimously votes to begin an impeachment trial against him. (AP) (Reuters)
  • 2027 Nigerian general election
    • The Federal High Court of Nigeria invalidates former vice president Atiku Abubakar's nomination as the African Democratic Congress candidate for the 2027 presidential election, ruling that the party's leadership was improperly constituted. (Reuters)
  • Constitutional crisis in Somalia, Controversies of Hassan Sheikh Mohamud
    • The Supreme Court of Somalia nullifies the amendments to the country's constitution, ruling that the term of president Hassan Sheikh Mohamud expired on 15 May 2026, while ordering new elections within 90 days. (AFP via Modern Ghana) (Somali Guardian)
  • Protests against the Russo-Ukrainian war, Belarusian involvement in the Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Belarus sentences Roman Catholic priest Anatoly Parakhnevich to three years in prison for opposing the war in Ukraine. (AP)

Sports

  • In golf, professional tour LIV Golf ceases operations after five seasons and liquidates its assets, following bankruptcy proceedings and the withdrawal of financial support from Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund and prospective investor BC Partners Credit. (AFP via France 24)

item.title: Current Events - November 08, 2026
item.description:
November 8, 2026 (2026-11-08) (Sunday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • Gaza war
      • Gaza humanitarian crisis
        • At least five people are killed, including four children, and several injured people are rescued after heavy rain and flooding caused a sandbank to collapse in Deir el-Balah, Gaza. (Al Jazeera)
    • Yemeni civil war
      • Houthi–Saudi conflict
        • Several floors of Aramco Tower, a skyscraper owned by Saudi Aramco located in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, are damaged after a Houthi ballistic missile is intercepted over the city by Saudi air defense systems. No casualties or injuries are reported. (Al Jazeera) (BBC News)
    • 2026 Iran war
      • Iranian state media reports that explosions are heard on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz after reporting that the U.S. military fired projectiles. (Middle East Eye)
    • Production is temporarily suspended at the Khor Mor gas field in Iraqi Kurdistan after a liquefied petroleum gas storage tank at the site is hit by a drone. No group claims responsibility for the attack. (Reuters) (AFP via South China Morning Post)
  • Mexican drug war
    • Mexican Navy personnel, working with intelligence from the National Intelligence Center and the United States Drug Enforcement Administration, arrest Rafael Álvarez Ayala, the alleged leader of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel cell "Los Rs", in Zapopan, Jalisco, Mexico. He is wounded in a shootout during the operation and is wanted on a Michoacán warrant for aggravated homicide. (Al Jazeera) (Infobae in Spanish) (El Financiero in Spanish)

Business and economy

  • Nvidia alleged spying scandal
    • NVIDIA announces it is opening an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang after American intelligence reported that a close associate of Huang was a spy for China. Huang admitted to an extramarital affair with the associate in a letter to the company earlier in the day. (BBC News) (The New York Times)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 El Ayyat train collision
    • A train derails near El Ayyat, Giza Governorate, Egypt, killing seven people and wounding 125 more. (AP) (Al Jazeera)
  • 2026 Indonesia wildfires
    • An Super Puma H-225 helicopter crashes in South Kalimantan during a forest firefighting mission, killing one person. (BBC)
  • Earthquakes in Japan
    • A Mw 5.7 earthquake strikes central Japan with its epicenter in Shizuoka Prefecture, while also affecting Aichi, Gifu, Nagano and Yamanashi prefectures. At least 22 people are injured. (AP) (NHK World-Japan)
  • The death toll from the boat capsizing yesterday off the coast of Kébémer, Louga, Senegal, increases to 39 people. (AFP via France 24)
  • A fire at a high-rise apartment building in Taiyuan, Shanxi, China, kills 14 people and leaves 25 others hospitalized. (Reuters) (South China Morning Post)
  • Three people are killed and more than 300 others are rescued from severe flooding in Erbil, Kurdistan Region, Iraq. (Shafaq)
  • A bus traveling towards Zagreb, Croatia, overturns on the A3 motorway, killing two people and injuring 20 others. (AP)

Law and crime

  • International Criminal Court investigation in Darfur
    • Former National Congress Party politician Ahmed Haroun, who is wanted by the International Criminal Court for genocide in Sudan's Darfur region during war, is detained by the Sudanese army. (AFP via Arab News)
  • The Maltese Civil Court orders four investment companies, including two from Malta and two from Luxembourg, to pay the Vatican Bank €24.1 million in damages over a 2013 deal involving the Kappa Fund. (Times of Malta) (Vatican News)

Politics and elections

  • Immigration to Spain
    • Authorities of El Hierro in the Canary Islands, Spain, declare a state of emergency following a surge of over 3,300 migrants and refugees arriving on the island this month. (Al Jazeera)
  • Gaza war protests
    • Three people are arrested as pro-Palestine protesters are confronted by pro-Israel counterprotesters in Rittenhouse Square, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, United States, amidst a boycott of six Jewish-owned restaurants targeted by a cycling club over their support of Israel. (NBC News)
    • More than 200,000 people march in Amsterdam, Netherlands, to protest against Israel's genocide in Gaza and the Dutch government's support of the Israeli military. (Al Jazeera)

Sports

  • 2026 Formula One World Championship, 2026 São Paulo Grand Prix
    • In Formula racing, Mercedes-Benz wins its ninth World Constructors' Championship after drivers George Russell and Kimi Antonelli finished fourth and fifth, respectively, at the São Paulo Grand Prix in Brazil. (Daily Tribune)
  • 2026 Major League Soccer season
    • In association football, Inter Miami player Lionel Messi is awarded the 2026 Golden Boot Award after scoring 26 goals in one season, becoming the first player in league history to win the award in consecutive years. (Al Jazeera)
  • 2026 NASCAR Cup Series
    • In stock car racing, Hendrick Motorsports' driver Kyle Larson wins his third career NASCAR Cup Series championship, becoming the first driver to win two consecutive championships since 2010. (AP)
  • 2026 PGA Tour
    • In golf, Blades Brown wins the 2026 World Wide Technology Championship in Los Cabos, Mexico, at 19 years and five months, becoming the youngest PGA Tour winner since 1931 and the fourth-youngest in its history. (AFP via The Philippine Star)

item.title: Current Events - November 01, 2026
item.description:
November 1, 2026 (2026-11-01) (Sunday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Gaza war
    • Israeli bombing of the Gaza Strip
      • Five civil police officers are killed in an Israeli airstrike in al-Mawasi, Rafah, Gaza Strip. Separately, three more Palestinians, including a four-year-old child, are killed in an airstrike on a building in Gaza City. (Al Jazeera)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026–2027 El Niño event
    • Bolivian president Rodrigo Paz declares a national state of emergency to mobilize resources before the super El Niño event peaks in November or December. (DW)
  • 2026 Palm Beach County Learjet 60 crash
    • Nine people are killed after a Learjet 60 business jet bound for The Bahamas crashes in Greenacres, Florida, United States. (Reuters)
  • Four workers are killed after entering a food waste tank at a hotel in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh, India. (Indian Express)

Health and environment

  • Air pollution in Delhi
    • The government of Delhi, India, introduces stricter pollution controls, including double parking fees, remote work arrangements, restrictions on high-emission vehicles, and bans on dust-producing construction, as PM2.5 levels reach 201 micrograms per cubic metre. (AFP via The Manila Times)

Law and crime

  • 2026 European unrest
    • 2026 Portuguese housing protests
      • Portuguese riot police dismantle protest camps in Lisbon's Rossio Square and Porto, arresting 13 people for refusing orders to disperse. Thirteen officers are injured, while activists say more than 30 protesters are also injured. (AFP) (Lianhe Zaobao)
  • 2026 Binance hack
    • The United States Federal Bureau of Investigation says North Korea orchestrated the hack and theft of over $6 billion of cryptocurrency from exchange Binance, facilitated through the Lazarus Group, which also hacked Dubai-based exchange Bybit last year. (DW)
  • 2026 Bangladesh garment workers protests
    • At least 20 people, including 4 police personnel, are injured in clashes between police and ready-made garment workers in Mirpur, Dhaka over low pay and the rising cost of living. In response, the government forms a wage board. (Al Jazeera) (Reuters) (UNB)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 anti-CEC protests
    • Thousands of people protest in New Delhi, India, to call for chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to resign due to changes to voter lists that allegedly disproportionately affect opposition parties. (AFP via France 24) (Al Jazeera)
  • 2026 Bulgarian presidential election
    • Bulgarians vote in the second round of presidential elections between incumbent Iliana Iotova and former acting prime minister Andrey Gyurov. Iotova is re-elected and Gyurov concedes after polls close. (AP) (DW)

Sports

  • 2026–27 ISU Grand Prix of Figure Skating
    • 2026 Skate Canada International
      • In figure skating, Japan's Mao Shimada wins the women's singles title at Skate Canada in her senior Grand Prix debut, finishing ahead of Estonia's Niina Petrõkina and American Isabeau Levito. (AFP via France 24)
  • 2026 Formula One World Championship
    • In open-wheel racing, Italian driver Kimi Antonelli, driving for Mercedes, wins the Formula One World Drivers' Championship after finishing third at the Mexico City Grand Prix, becoming the youngest Drivers' Champion at the age of 20 years and 68 days. (ESPN)
  • 2026 MotoGP World Championship
    • In motorcycle racing, Yamaha withdraws from the Qatar Grand Prix next week, citing company-wide travel restrictions following its assessment of the Middle Eastern crisis. (AFP via The Manila Times)
  • 2026 NFL season
    • In American football, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers refuse to complete a pass during its 16-0 victory against the rival Atlanta Falcons in Week 8, becoming the first National Football League team to win a game without completing a pass since the Buffalo Bills did so in 1974. (NBC News)
  • 2026 New York City Marathon
    • Swedish long-distance runner Andreas Almgren wins the 55th edition of the New York City Marathon in New York City, New York, U.S., during his first debut. (The Athletic via The New York Times)
  • 2026 Mamoré-Uberlândia football match incident
    • In association football, a match between U20 clubs EC Mamoré and Uberlândia EC in Minas Gerais, Brazil, is abandoned after referees handed out 53 red cards, including to 43 players and 10 club officials, following a massive brawl, setting the world record for the most red cards given in a single match. (ESPN)

item.title: Current Events - October 31, 2026
item.description:
October 31, 2026 (2026-10-31) (Saturday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • 2026 Bangladesh garment workers protests
    • At least 30 people are injured, including police and dozens of factories suspend operations after thousands of garment workers clash with police across Gazipur and Dhaka while demanding an inflation-linked minimum monthly wage amid the rising cost of living. (Prothom Alo)

Disasters and accidents

  • Human trafficking in the Netherlands
    • The Dutch military police and coast guard rescue 38 people from a rubber boat adrift off the coast of Breskens, Zeeland, and detain two people on suspicion of people smuggling. (AP)

International relations

  • Polish constitutional crisis, China–Poland relations, Poland–Romania relations
    • Polish Constitutional Tribunal crisis
      • Suspension of Bogdan Święczkowski
        • Poland's ambassador to Romania, Paweł Soloch, and Poland's ambassador to China, Jakub Kumoch, resign from their positions in protest of the suspension of Polish Constitutional Tribunal president Bogdan Święczkowski. (24 Kanal) (Firstpost)

Law and crime

  • Gaza war protests in the United Kingdom
    • Metropolitan Police arrest 139 people outside the United States embassy in London, United Kingdom, during a protest supporting Palestine Action, which is designated as a proscribed terrorist organisation. (AP)
  • Trafficking of Chinese nationals to scam centers abroad, Human trafficking in Madagascar
    • Madagascar's justice ministry announces dismantling 13 Chinese-run scam centers since August, linked to 148 Chinese nationals who had previously operated scam centers in Cambodia, and who might have been involved in trafficking Africans to commit fraud. The 148 Chinese are extradited to China. (AFP)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 European unrest
    • 2026 French student protests
      • Protests are held across France for the third consecutive weekend. (AP) (France 24)
    • Protests are held in 34 cities across Germany against the high cost of livings and wars. Clashes with the police erupt in Frankfurt, Berlin, Cologne and Hamburg. In Frankfurt, shops are looted, with several people being arrested. (BBC News)
    • Riots erupt in Zurich and Basel, Switzerland, with fires reported. (Swiss Info)
    • Clashes erupt in The Hague, Netherlands, in a youth-led protest, with 34 people arrested. (NL Times)

Sports

  • 2026–27 ISU Grand Prix of Figure Skating
    • 2026 Skate Canada International
      • In figure skating, France's Kevin Aymoz wins the men's singles title at Skate Canada in Kelowna, British Columbia, overtaking Japan's Rio Nakata and becoming the second-oldest men's Grand Prix champion at age 29. (NBC Sports)
  • 2026 Breeders' Cup
    • 2026 Breeders' Cup Classic
      • In thoroughbred horse racing, thoroughbred racehorse Sovereignty wins the Breeders' Cup classic at the Keeneland racetrack in Lexington, Kentucky, U.S. (ESPN) (The Blood-Horse)
  • 2026 Summer Youth Olympics
    • The 2026 Summer Youth Olympics opens in Dakar, Senegal, marking the first IOC event in Africa. (AFP via France 24)
  • 2026 WNBA Finals
    • In women's basketball, the Golden State Valkyries defeat the Atlanta Dream 68–63 in game seven to win their first WNBA championship. Gabby Williams is named MVP. (AFP) (AP)

item.title: Current Events - November 07, 2026
item.description:
November 7, 2026 (2026-11-07) (Saturday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Sudanese civil war
    • Kordofan campaign
      • Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) says that they have recaptured the town of Iyal Bakhit in West Kordofan, Sudan. The SAF also reportedly downs a Rapid Support Forces drone. (Sudan Tribune)
  • 2026 Kraków shooting
    • Six people are killed and 15 more injured in a drive-by mass shooting in the center of Kraków, Poland. The perpetrator, who also killed his parents and his sister at their home in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski, is wounded by police and arrested. (Reuters)
  • Houthi–Saudi conflict
    • Saudi airstrikes hit homes near Sanaa, Yemen, killing at least 27 people and wounding 36 others. (AP)
  • Colombian conflict
    • A drone strike of unknown origin is launched against a military base in Santa Rosa del Sur, Bolívar Department, Colombia, killing three soldiers and wounding 16 more. (AP)
  • Nigerian bandit conflict
    • A family of twelve are killed in an arson attack during a bandit raid in Maradun, Zamfara State, Nigeria. Seven others are kidnapped. (Nigerian Info)

Disasters and accidents

  • Twenty-one people are killed and one person has been rescued after a migrant boat sinks off the coast of Kebemer, Louga region, Senegal. (Xinhua)
  • At least 12 people, mostly bus passengers, are killed and 13 others are injured in a multiple-vehicle collision near Atalaya, Valparaíso Region, Chile. (AFP via The Sun)
  • Nine people are killed and five others are injured when a truck collides with a minibus in Özalp, Van Province, Turkey. (Daily Sabah)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 French student protests
    • Unions, yellow vests protesters, and student protesters hold a fourth consecutive weekend of protests across France with about 146,000 participants. (AFP) (Al Jazeera)
  • 2026 Israeli legislative election
    • Israeli president Isaac Herzog selects Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot to attempt to form a coalition government following inconclusive Knesset elections. Eisenkot will have 28 days to secure sufficient support in the Knesset. (ABC News Australia) (The Times of Israel)
  • 2026 New Zealand general election
    • New Zealanders vote to elect 120 members of the House of Representatives, with 11 additional overhang seats. National Party leader Christopher Luxon and Labour leader Chris Hipkins both seek reappointment as the country's prime minister. Preliminary results see Labour lead in the popular vote and the Nationals having the most amount of seats, with special votes yet to be counted. (AP) (RNZ)

Sports

  • In sailing, Frenchman Tom Laperche wins the 2026 Route du Rhum in a record six days, 13 hours, 27 minutes and 40 seconds, beating Charles Caudrelier's 2022 time by six hours and 19 minutes. (AFP) (Reuters)

item.title: Current Events - November 09, 2026
item.description:
November 9, 2026 (2026-11-09) (Monday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • 2026 Iran war
    • United Kingdom involvement in the 2026 Iran war
      • The Wall Street Journal reports that the United States has evacuated aircraft from the RAF Mildenhall base in the United Kingdom, citing threats from Iran. (Reuters)
  • 2026 Kraków shooting
    • The 24-year-old man responsible for the drive-by mass shooting at the Main Square in Kraków, Poland, two days ago, which killed six people and injured 16 others, dies at a hospital after being seriously wounded in a shootout with police. (Al Jazeera)

Arts and culture

  • 2026 Booker Prize
    • English author M. John Harrison wins the 2026 Booker Prize for his post-apocalyptic novel The End of Everything. (The Guardian)
  • The Pitt Rivers Museum in Oxford, England, United Kingdom, returns the remains of 39 Naga people, collected during the British Raj, to a delegation from Nagaland, India, following six years of discussions over repatriation. (AFP via France 24)

Business and economy

  • 2026 Paraguay banking crisis
    • Paraguayan president Pedro Alliana appoints economist Jorge Schreiner to lead the central bank following Ueno Bank's collapse. The Senate approves Schreiner's appointment. (Reuters)
  • China–United States trade war
    • The Chinese commerce ministry extends the suspension of export restrictions on certain rare earths, industrial diamonds, and lithium battery technology to January 10, 2027, amid ongoing trade negotiations with the United States. (Reuters)
  • The South Korean Fair Trade Commission issues fines of ₩331.1 billion (US$247 million) for Woowa Brothers and ₩300.8 billion ($222 million) for Coupang, finding that their food-delivery platforms restricted competition by requiring restaurants to match rival platforms' terms. (AFP via France 24)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Aliağa factory explosion
    • Seventeen people are killed and twelve others are injured in an explosion at a factory in Aliağa, Turkey. (BBC News)
  • At least five people are reported missing after two boats collide off the coast of Trinidad. Search and rescue operations are underway by the Trinbagonian Coast Guard. (AP)

International relations

  • Cyprus problem
    • Cypriot president Nikos Christodoulides and Northern Cypriot president Tufan Erhürman agree to establish two additional crossings across the United Nations Buffer Zone in Cyprus and hold further peace negotiations. (Reuters)

Law and crime

  • English actor Russell Brand is sentenced to 10 years and 6 months imprisonment for one rape and three counts of sexual assault. (CNN) (RTÉ News)

Politics and elections

  • Censorship in Russia
    • Russian independent newspaper Novaya Gazeta ceases operations as it closes its offices in Moscow, citing pressure from Russian authorities and security services, including restrictions on its operations, loss of media registration, and blocked donations. (AP)

Sports

  • In college football, the College Football Playoff announces it will expand from 12 to 24 teams starting in the 2027 season. (ESPN)

item.title: Current Events - November 02, 2026
item.description:
November 2, 2026 (2026-11-02) (Monday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • Gaza war
      • 2026 West Bank lockdown
        • Israeli forces withdraw from areas around Hebron in the occupied West Bank after a multi-day operation following the killing of two Israeli soldiers at a checkpoint. (AFP via RFI) (Al Jazeera)
    • 2026 Iran war
      • The United States military carries out airstrikes on Iranian targets across the Strait of Hormuz after Iranian surface-to-air missiles attack American aircraft in the Strait. (Al Jazeera) (AP)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war, Zaporizhzhia strikes
      • Russian forces drop at least nine bombs on a school building serving as a civilian shelter and humanitarian aid distribution centre in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia Oblast, Ukraine, killing at least 33 people and leaving 50 others missing. (CNN)
  • Haitian conflict
    • Salvadoran military intervention in Haiti
      • Salvadoran, Haitian, and Gang Suppression Force soldiers launch an offensive in Plain of the Cul-de-Sac which extends from Haiti to the Dominican Republic, killing at least a dozen gang members. (EFE in Spanish)
  • Mexican drug war
    • Infighting in the Sinaloa Cartel
      • Three people are killed and five more injured in two separated mass shootings at two drug rehabilitation centers in Mazatlán, Sinaloa, Mexico. (La Jornada in Spanish)
  • Sudanese civil war
    • War crimes in the Sudanese civil war
      • The Rapid Support Forces launches drone strikes against three distribution stations in Sudan's Kassala and Northern states. (Sudan Tribune)
  • Colombian conflict
    • A truck bomb explodes near a military base in Planadas, Tolima Department, Colombia, killing four people, including a baby, and wounding several others. (BBC News) (Reuters)
  • Peruvian security crisis
    • An unidentified person throws an IED bomb at the home of Villa El Salvador mayor-elect Marcelino Huamán Cano in Lima, Peru, while he was with his family, causing property damage but no reported injuries. (Perú.21 in Spanish)
  • Somali Civil War
    • Uganda begins withdrawing its troops from Somalia, planning to remove all personnel deployed under bilateral and African Union missions by the end of 2027, ending nearly two decades of operations. (AFP via Arab News)

Business and economy

  • Rwanda–United States relations, South Africa–United States relations
    • The United States announces the suspensions of Rwanda and South Africa from duty-free trade benefits under the African Growth and Opportunity Act beginning January 1, 2027, citing trade barriers, human rights concerns, and threats to U.S. interests. (Reuters)

Disasters and accidents

  • Eight people are killed after they were electrocuted when a vehicle comes into contact with a high-voltage power line in Jhunjhunu, Rajasthan, India. (Xinhua)

Health and environment

  • The United States Food and Drug Administration approves the first generic version of lenacapavir, a twice-yearly HIV prevention injection expected to cost about US$40 annually in 120 low- and middle-income countries. (AFP via France 24)

Law and crime

  • 2026 French supermarket refrigerator hack
    • A second wave of cyberattacks target freezers and refrigerators in supermarkets in multiple European countries, causing them to overheat and spoil. (Reuters)

Politics and elections

  • The Spanish interior ministry reportedly deports 16 migrants, including those from Bangladesh, Cameroon, Nigeria, Senegal, and Yemen, from Ceuta to Morocco following the migrant crisis in July. (The New Arab)

item.title: Current Events - October 30, 2026
item.description:
October 30, 2026 (2026-10-30) (Friday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • 2026 Iran war
      • 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
        • Oman rescues 25 crew members from a burning Panamanian-flagged oil tanker in the Strait of Hormuz. The Iranian military confirms it was a result of attempting to pass through an unauthorised route. (Al Jazeera)
    • Houthi–Saudi conflict, Saudi-led intervention in the Yemeni civil war, Yemeni civil war
      • The Saudi Arabia-led coalition announces it intercepted a drone allegedly launched by the Houthis towards the Mecca region, which the Houthis deny. (Al Jazeera)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Peace negotiations in the Russo-Ukrainian war, Blockade of Oleshky
      • Civilian evacuations commence in Oleshky, Ukraine, as a humanitarian convoy arrives in the Russian-held and besieged city, as part of a local ceasefire brokered by the United States. (The Guardian)
  • Operation Southern Spear
    • The Venezuelan and the United States militaries carry out a joint operation with airstrikes and drones against an alleged hideout belonging to the National Liberation Army in Apure, Venezuela, killing at least 23 people and wounding dozens more. (El Pais)

Business and economy

  • Russian independent newspaper Novaya Gazeta announces plans to cease operations on 9 November, citing pressure from Russian authorities. (Reuters)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Uttarakhand helicopter crash
    • Six people are killed when their helicopter crashes near Joshimath, Uttarakhand, India. (AFP via Daily Sun) (The Times of India)
  • Five children and two adults are killed, five other people are injured, and four are missing after flash floods caused by heavy rainfall in eastern Syria. (Reuters)

Law and crime

  • Leongatha mushroom murders
    • The Court of Appeal of Victoria, Australia, rejects Erin Patterson's appeal against her murder convictions and removes her 33-year parole eligibility, effectively imposing life imprisonment without parole for killing three relatives with death cap mushrooms in 2023. (AFP)
  • 2026 Binance hack
    • Cryptocurrency exchange Binance confirms that assets worth US$6.3 billion were stolen, making it the largest cryptocurrency theft in history. (Bloomberg News) (Reuters) (Engadget)
  • The Swiss supreme court upholds a 20-year jail sentence for former Liberian rebel commander Alieu Kosiah after he was found guilty in 2021 for atrocities committed during the First Liberian Civil War, but overturns a conviction for crimes against humanity. (Al Jazeera)

Politics and elections

  • 2015–present Polish rule-of-law crisis
    • 2026 Polish Constitutional Tribunal crisis
      • Polish police enter the Constitutional Tribunal following the suspension of its president Bogdan Święczkowski, announced by judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska. The tribunal describes the suspension as a coup d'état, while three protesters in support of PiS are detained after breaching the tribunal's fence. (Euronews)
      • Polish justice minister Waldemar Żurek requests stripping the tribunal's president and vice president Bartłomiej Sochański of their immunity from prosecution in order to charge them. President Karol Nawrocki cancels his trip to Senegal due to the situation and lands back in Poland. (AP) (BBC News)
  • 2026 European unrest
    • 2026 Italian unrest
      • A general strike and multiple protests are held across Italy against the rising cost of living and prime minister Giorgia Meloni's government, with clashes breaking out in multiple cities. (CNN) (DW)

Sports

  • 2026 Breeders' Cup
    • In thoroughbred horse racing, race horse Sun Goddess dominates the Juvenile Fillies Turf at the Keeneland racetrack in Lexington, Kentucky, United States, during the Breeders' Cup. Additionally, Emphatic wins the Juvenile Fillies. (The Blood-Horse) (Sky Sports)
  • International sporting sanctions during the Russian invasion of Ukraine
    • In ice hockey, the Court of Arbitration for Sports rules that Russian teams must be allowed to take part in all international tournaments, overturning previous International Ice Hockey Federation decisions. (DW)

item.title: Current Events - November 06, 2026
item.description:
November 6, 2026 (2026-11-06) (Friday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Kivu conflict
    • Allied Democratic Forces insurgency
      • The death toll from an armed attack yesterday by suspected Allied Democratic Forces militants on several villages in North Kivu, eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, rises to 33. (AA)
  • Houthi–Saudi conflict
    • Saudi Arabia launches an airstrike against a market in Taiz Governorate, Yemen, killing 30 people and wounding eight more. (AP)
  • Crime in Guatemala
    • Politician Julio Portillo and three police officers are killed in an assassination shooting in Río Hondo, Zacapa Department, Guatemala, by unknown gunmen. (Al Jazeera)
  • Mexican drug war
    • Three gunmen were killed after an encounter against authorities in the ejido Las Trancas, Navolato, Sinaloa, México. (El Universal in Spanish)
    • Edgar Aarón Vázquez, founder and leader of the Nuevo Imperio cartel, is killed in an operation in Naucalpan, State of Mexico. He was implicated in the murder of a federal agent, as well as kidnapping, extortion, homicide, dispossession of property, money laundering, fuel theft, and drug trafficking to the United States and Canada. (Excélsior in Spanish)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Indonesia wildfires, Australia–Indonesia relations
    • Australia deploys a C-130 Hercules aircraft, a Cessna Citation aircraft, and 20 personnel to help extinguish wildfires in East Kalimantan, Indonesia. (AFP)
  • Two people are killed and 16 injured in a bus crash in Lent, Ain, France. (AP) (Le Monde)

Health and environment

  • Measles resurgence in the United States
    • The United States Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reports 5,182 measles cases in 2026, the country's highest annual total since 1991. State health agencies report at least eight measles-related deaths. (AFP via France 24)
  • The Standing Committee of the National People's Congress of China adopts a law regulating Chinese research, tourism, shipping, and other activities in Antarctica, requiring environmental safeguards, waste management, and permits subject to safety conditions. (Reuters)

Law and crime

  • 1MDB scandal
    • Malaysia's UMNO party pays a RM50-million (US$12 million) fine for imprisoned former prime minister Najib Razak, fulfilling a condition of his royal pardon. The Attorney-General's Chambers subsequently seeks to delay his transfer to house arrest. (AFP via France 24)
  • 2026 European unrest, Opposition to AI data centers
    • At least 100 people are arrested by police after protesters break into and temporarily occupy a construction site for a Microsoft data center in Sloterdijk, Amsterdam, Netherlands, during an anti-data-center rally. (Al Jazeera) (Reuters)
  • Shakahola Forest incident
    • Kenyan cult leader Paul Mackenzie is sentenced to 200 years in prison for the mass murder of children. (Reuters)
  • American cinematographer Thomas Markle is arrested in Tampa, Florida, over allegations of possessing child sexual abuse material. (BBC News) (CBS News)
  • The Colombian border control agency expels 80 Venezuelan nationals suspected of criminal activity, including theft, drug trafficking, and extortion. (AFP via France 24)
  • Au Kam San, a former pro-democracy legislator of Macau, is convicted in a closed-door trial of "subversion against the political power of the state" and sentenced to 12 years and 6 months in prison. It is the first conviction under the Macau National Security Law, which was revised by lawmakers in 2023 to broaden its scope and to allow for closed-door trials. (BBC News)
  • The High Court of Tanzania acquits Chadema chairperson Tundu Lissu of treason but sentences him to four years in prison for incitement related to statements opposing the 2025 general election results. (AFP via France 24)
  • A court in Istanbul, Turkey, orders the detention of legislator and former family minister Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya pending trial on charges of violating capital markets legislation and membership in a criminal organization amid an investigation into investment fund manipulation. (AP)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Paraguay banking crisis
    • The Paraguayan Senate unanimously removes Santiago Peña as the country's president over alleged conflicts of interest involving Ueno Bank, whose accounts the central bank froze. Congress postpones consideration of Peña's resignation to allow impeachment proceedings. (AFP) (Reuters)
    • The Public Prosecutor's Office orders the arrest of Santiago Peña, who is placed under house arrest. (UPI)
    • Vice President Pedro Alliana is sworn in as the interim president of Paraguay. (Reuters)
  • King Philippe of Belgium refuses Bart De Wever's resignation as the prime minister, telling him to continue with budget negotiations. (Euronews) (Xinhua)
